translationRepairs: His other attacks on Zeng Zhao, Wang Di, Zhang Tingjian, Jia Yi, Li Zhaoxu, Lü Xizhe, Fan Chunli, Su Shi, and others were not always endorsed by public opinion.
His other attacks on Zeng Zhao, Wang Di, Zhang Tingjian, Jia Yi, Li Zhaoqi, Lü Xizhe, Fan Chunli, Su Shi, and others were not always endorsed by public opinion.
李昭玘 is Li Zhaoqi (玘 qi), not "Zhaoxu".

When the Prince of Jiyang, Zong Jing, asked to elevate a concubine to wife, Cisheng argued that he had set aside ritual propriety by virtue of his princely rank and was bringing disgrace on the dynasty.

When the Prince of Jiyang, Zongjing, asked to elevate a concubine to wife, Cisheng argued that he had set aside ritual propriety by virtue of his princely rank and was bringing disgrace on the dynasty.
宗景 is the single given name Zongjing of an imperial clansman (surname Zhao), not "Zong Jing".
Xiang Zonghui and Zong Liang also secretly aid Jing.
Xiang Zonghui and Xiang Zongliang also secretly aid Jing.
宗良 shares the surname Xiang with 向宗回 (the "two Xiangs" of s0104); his given name is Zongliang, not "Zong Liang".
Lu Tao, courtesy name Yuanjun, was a native of Chengdu.
Lü Tao, courtesy name Yuanjun, was a native of Chengdu.
呂陶 is Lü Tao (呂 Lü), not "Lu".

Cai Que, Han Zong, Zhang Can, and Zhang Dun—in the previous reign they worked hand in glove with petty men, pushing policies that robbed the people and harmed the realm, so that the sovereign's grace could not reach those below;

Cai Que, Han Zong, Zhang Zao, and Zhang Dun—in the previous reign they worked hand in glove with petty men, pushing policies that robbed the people and harmed the realm, so that the sovereign's grace could not reach those below;
張璪 is Zhang Zao (璪 zao), not "Zhang Can".
An Yan and Li Qingchen fawn and drift among them as well, waiting to see where power lies before they commit themselves.
An Tao and Li Qingchen fawn and drift among them as well, waiting to see where power lies before they commit themselves.
安燾 is An Tao (燾 tao), not "An Yan".
Ren Boryu argued that Tingjian's personal integrity was sound and that he should not be stripped of his censorial post.
Ren Boyu argued that Tingjian's personal integrity was sound and that he should not be stripped of his censorial post.
任伯雨 is Ren Boyu, not "Boryu".
Boryu protested again, asking that Tingjian's memorial be referred outside the court to test his claims, so remonstrators would not be intimidated by the Three Departments.
Boyu protested again, asking that Tingjian's memorial be referred outside the court to test his claims, so remonstrators would not be intimidated by the Three Departments.

Wielding power to settle private scores, they stirred up the moral order of ruler and subject, father and son, unsettling the realm so that even Emperor Shenzong's legacy of orderly succession could not shine as it should.

Wielding power to settle private scores, they stirred up the moral order of ruler and subject, father and son, unsettling the realm so that even Emperor Zhezong (Tailing) could not fully realize the beauty of carrying on his father's work.
泰陵 is the mausoleum name of Zhezong, not Shenzong.
When Prince of Cai Wang Si's clerk was prosecuted on vague charges of seditious speech, Gongwang pleaded forcefully for mercy; he was sent out as prefect of Huaiyang Army.
When the clerk of Si, Prince of Cai, was prosecuted on vague charges of seditious speech, Gongwang pleaded forcefully for mercy; he was sent out as prefect of Huaiyang Army.
蔡王似 is the imperial prince Si (surname Zhao), Prince of Cai, not a man named "Wang Si".

Jia Yi, Cen Xiangqiu, Feng Ji, Zhang Lei, Huang Tingjian, Gong Yuan, Chao Buzhi, Liu Tanglao, and Li Zhaoji are all men of talent who could serve — their only fault is that their records look slightly suspect.

Jia Yi, Cen Xiangqiu, Feng Ji, Zhang Lei, Huang Tingjian, Gong Yuan, Chao Buzhi, Liu Tanglao, and Li Zhaoqi are all men of talent who could serve — their only fault is that their records look slightly suspect.
李昭玘 is Li Zhaoqi (玘 qi), not "Zhaoji".
He memorialized Emperor Huizong: "I have been instructed, together with Ren Boryu, to examine Han Zhongyan's recommendations of Yuanyou officials.
He memorialized Emperor Huizong: "I have been instructed, together with Ren Boyu, to examine Han Zhongyan's recommendations of Yuanyou officials.
任伯雨 is Ren Boyu, not "Boryu".
When Cai Bian sought to demote Boryu and others, You was included; he was banished under registration to Lizhou and later moved to Guizhou.
When Cai Bian sought to demote Boyu and others, You was included; he was banished under registration to Lizhou and later moved to Guizhou.
Anmin answered, "When men like you rise high, the realm's fate is clear. I will go back to the hills — why should I still argue right and wrong with you?
Anmin answered, "With Chuhou in high office, the realm's fate is clear. I will go back to the hills — why should I still argue right and wrong with you?
處厚 is An Dun's courtesy name Chuhou, used to address him, not "men like you".
Early in Yuanyou, Li Chang, Sun Jue, Fan Bailu, Su Shi, and Xianyu Zuo jointly recommended him; he was promoted to assistant in the Court of Judicial Review and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Early in Yuanyou, Li Chang, Sun Jue, Fan Bailu, Su Shi, and Xianyu Shen jointly recommended him; he was promoted to assistant in the Court of Judicial Review and the Court of State Ceremonial.
鮮于侁 is Xianyu Shen (侁 shen), not "Zuo"; 鴻臚 is the Court of State Ceremonial, not of Imperial Sacrifices.
When he reached Chuz, he personally handled minor business every day.
When he reached Chuzhou, he personally handled minor business every day.
Truncated place name: 滁 is Chuzhou.

Kui drove Zhang Dun, Cai Jing, and Cai Bian from office—enough to relieve somewhat the rage of people across the empire; yet Jing and Bian fell only to rise again, removed only to return—blind at the edge of collapse; with so dull a ruler, what could one say?

Que drove Zhang Dun, Cai Jing, and Cai Bian from office—enough to relieve somewhat the rage of people across the empire; yet Jing and Bian fell only to rise again, removed only to return—blind at the edge of collapse; with so dull a ruler, what could one say?
𡙇 is Gong Que (rendered "Que" elsewhere in the chapter), not "Kui".
